books.section: Topic 8.2 The Cold War from 1945 to 1980
Truman and the Beginning of the Cold War (1945-1953)

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question; facts from the grounding books.
stimulus.text: Original secondary passage: The United States came out of World War II as the world's strongest power, while Europe's great powers lay in ruins. American leaders believed the peace had failed after World War I because nations had acted alone. This time they built a different order: a new United Nations to settle disputes together, American aid to rebuild friendly nations, and lasting alliances to deter aggression.

source: original; stimulus is an original secondary passage written for this question; facts from the grounding books
stem: Taken together, the United Nations, the Marshall Plan, and NATO show which of the following about the United States after World War II?

options.text: The United States had become weaker than it was before the war and needed other nations to protect it.
options.misconception: America emerged from the war as the strongest power on earth, not as a weak nation needing protection.

options.text: The United States had decided to fight a war against the Soviet Union as soon as possible.
options.misconception: The UN, the Marshall Plan, and NATO were built to prevent war and contain communism, not to start a war.

options.text: The United States had returned to the foreign policy of the 1920s.
options.misconception: The 1920s meant keeping distance; the new institutions meant permanent American leadership abroad.

options.text: The United States had accepted permanent leadership of a world order it helped to build.

rationales.A: The United States came out of the war stronger, not weaker. It was the world's strongest power, and others needed its aid and protection.
rationales.B: None of the three aimed at starting a war with the Soviet Union. They were built to deter attack and contain communism without fighting.
rationales.C: The 1920s policy was to stay out of world bodies and alliances. These three institutions did the opposite, binding America to the world.
rationales.D: The United Nations, the Marshall Plan, and NATO were all lasting systems with the United States at their center. Background from the books: building them meant America had accepted permanent leadership of the non-communist world.
rationales.general:
1. List the three pieces. A United Nations to settle disputes, Marshall Plan aid to rebuild friendly nations, and NATO to deter attack.
2. Ask what they share. Background from the books: each one puts the United States at the center of a lasting system, not a one-time act.
3. Ask what changed from the 1920s. Background from the books: after World War I, America stayed out of world bodies; after World War II, it built them and led them.
4. Name the new role. The United States became the permanent leader of the non-communist world, by design and not by accident.
Remember: institutions outlast speeches, and these three show a country that meant to stay in charge.
